original_question: For each natural number n, let R_n^infty be the maximum Banach-Mazur distance between an n-dimensional Banach space X and l_infty^n. Determine the asymptotic behavior of R_n^infty as n tends to infinity.
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 1 (“Distance from the cube” – A. Pełczyński).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem from the paper: for each dimension n, it considers the extremal Banach–Mazur distance from an n-dimensional Banach space to \ell_\infty^n, and it asks for the asymptotic behavior as n\to\infty. That is exactly the mathematical content of the paper’s Problem 1 in Section 2.
missing_details: The paper’s notation is R_\infty^n, not R_n^\infty.
A stand-alone version should define the Banach–Mazur distance explicitly: d(X,Y)=\inf\{\|T\|\,\|T^{-1}\|: T\!:X\to Y \text{ is a linear isomorphism}\}.
It should say that X ranges over all n-dimensional Banach spaces (equivalently, over all n-dimensional Banach-space isomorphism classes) over the same scalar field as \ell_\infty^n.
It should identify \ell_\infty^n as the classical n-dimensional sup-norm space.
If one wants full paper-faithfulness, it helps to preserve the paper’s framing and attribution: this is Problem 1, titled “Distance from the cube,” and attributed to A. Pełczyński.

The nearby context in the paper also records the best known lower and upper bounds available there and explains that the problem is included because the known nontrivial upper bounds use variants of the Sauer–Shelah lemma; this is context rather than part of the formal statement, but it is part of the paper’s intent.
refined_question: For each n\in\mathbb{N}, let R_\infty^n:=\max\{d(X,\ell_\infty^n): X \text{ is an } n\text{-dimensional Banach space over the same scalar field as } \ell_\infty^n\}, where \ell_\infty^n is the classical n-dimensional space with the sup norm and d(X,Y):=\inf\{\|T\|\,\|T^{-1}\|: T\!:X\to Y \text{ is a linear isomorphism}\} is the Banach\u2013Mazur distance. Determine the asymptotic behavior of R_\infty^n as n\to\infty.
justification: The draft clearly targets the paper’s first open problem in the section “Distance from the cube,” not some broader neighboring question. In Section 2 the authors first recall the definition of the Banach–Mazur distance, then define R_\infty^n, and immediately state Problem 1: determine the asymptotic behavior of R_\infty^n as n tends to infinity. The introduction also lists “Distance from the cube” as the first featured open problem, confirming the match. The surrounding paragraph adds contextual information (known lower/upper bounds and the Sauer–Shelah motivation), but the official target is simply Section 2, Problem 1. The only real defects in the draft are the reversed notation and the absence of the explicit definition of d(X,Y), plus the implicit scope of the maximization.
